title: GEO Pitch Red-Flag Auditor
note: Spec/data file for the artifact described in ARTIFACT-BRIEF.md. This is structured content only, no HTML/JS is implemented here. This tool evaluates a GEO AGENCY'S PITCH (its claims), not the reader's own website, and never computes, displays or implies a numeric score of any kind — a fake 'AI visibility score with no disclosed inputs' is itself one of the ten red flags this tool checks for. A pitch labelled 'Weissmann' receives no special treatment in the logic or the visuals.

pitchLabel.note: Never request a company's registered name, a personal name, an email address, or any other identifying detail.

claims.label: They promised a specific number or date for an AI citation (e.g. "live in ChatGPT within 30/60 days", "triple your AI visibility this quarter").
claims.whyItMatters: No one, including Weissmann, can guarantee an AI citation. AI assistants retrieve from a live index and a model the vendor does not control; Google itself will not guarantee inclusion in its own AI Overviews even when every best practice is met.

claims.label: They claimed Google (or another AI provider) requires special AI-only schema, markup, or a "compliance tag".
claims.whyItMatters: Google's own developer documentation states no special AI-only schema or markup is required to appear in AI features. No comparable requirement exists for ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity.

claims.label: They referenced a "proprietary GEO algorithm" or "secret ranking signals" they would not plainly describe.
claims.whyItMatters: The real mechanics, answer-first writing, entity consistency, structured data, crawler access, are public and taught for free by credible sources; a method too secret to explain is usually a method that does not exist.

claims.label: Their pricing is pay-per-citation or pay-only-if-cited.
claims.whyItMatters: This pricing model only works if the vendor can reliably produce citations on demand, which no one can guarantee, so it quietly assumes the exact promise a credible vendor should not be making.

claims.label: Their case studies are built only from an AI chat screenshot, with no reproducible method shown.
claims.whyItMatters: The same prompt asked minutes later from a different account can return a different answer; a credible case study documents specific site changes and a stated measurement method, not one lucky screenshot.

claims.label: They offered a proprietary "AI visibility score" with no disclosed inputs.
claims.whyItMatters: Presented as an objective diagnostic, this usually functions as a lead-generation device; a transparent audit lists concrete, checkable items instead of a single invented number.

claims.label: They pushed urgency about a "narrow window before competitors catch up" with no specifics.
claims.whyItMatters: Reasonable as an offhand comment, risky as the basis for a same-week signature; ask exactly what expires, and why, in writing.

claims.label: Their quote never mentions your existing SEO, content quality, or crawler accessibility.
claims.whyItMatters: GEO builds on the same technical and content foundations as SEO, not instead of them; a quote that skips your starting point is pricing a number, not a project.

claims.label: They were vague about which AI systems and which languages are actually in scope.
claims.whyItMatters: A Swiss business typically needs German, French or Italian alongside English; vagueness on language scope may mean a generic, English-only package resold under a Swiss label.

claims.label: They pushed you to sign before you could verify any earlier claim independently.
claims.whyItMatters: A genuine specialist's own published pages should already demonstrate the same writing and structure it is proposing to sell you.

answerOptions.label: No, they did not say this

scoringRule.note: No numeric score of any kind. Purely a rule-based, plain-language read.
scoringRule.criticalRule: If ANY claim with severity 'critical' is answered 'yes', overall read = 'high' regardless of all other answers. Show both critical claims' whyItMatters text regardless of which one triggered it.
scoringRule.cautionRule: Only evaluated if no critical claim is 'yes'. Count claims with severity 'caution' answered 'yes': 0-1 -> 'low', 2-3 -> 'moderate', 4+ -> 'high'.
scoringRule.notSureRule: Answers of 'not_sure' never count toward either rule. Every claim left 'not_sure' is collected into a separate stillUnknown list.
scoringRule.allNotSureRule: If all ten claims are 'not_sure', show no risk read at all — only the stillUnknown list (all ten) and the prompt to answer at least one claim.

riskReadCopy.high_critical: High concern — these are not judgment calls.
riskReadCopy.high_caution: High concern — multiple independent warning signs are present.
riskReadCopy.moderate: Moderate concern — work through the five due-diligence questions before signing.
riskReadCopy.low: Low concern — still confirm every answer before signing.
riskReadCopy.insufficient: Answer at least one claim to see a concern read for this pitch.

alwaysFalseReminder.note: Static box, always visible regardless of any answer given.
alwaysFalseReminder.text: Two claims are false for any GEO vendor, always: a guaranteed AI citation, and a claim that an AI-only schema is required by Google or any other AI provider.

dueDiligenceQuestions: Show me one recent page you rewrote for a client, before and after, not a chat screenshot, the actual page.
Which specific assistants and which languages are in scope, and how will you check them over time?
What happens on the invoice in a quarter where no citation appears anywhere?
Who reviews my crawlability and technical SEO baseline first, and can I see that report before any GEO work starts?
If I apply these same questions to your own pitch, will you sit through that conversation?

followUpMessage.template: Before we go further, could you clarify: {claimLabels}? And could you answer directly: {selectedQuestions}?
followUpMessage.selectionRule: Include all five dueDiligenceQuestions if more than three claims are 'yes' or 'not_sure' combined; otherwise include only the questions most relevant to the flagged claims (e.g. pay_per_citation -> the invoice question; vague_scope -> the languages/assistants question).

copyButton.label: Copy message
copyButton.fallback: manual-select, no visible error thrown on failure

noSpecialTreatmentRule: The optional pitch label (including 'Weissmann') is never read by any logic branch and never changes styling, wording, or the risk read. Identical treatment regardless of label.

errorStates.behavior: Show only the full stillUnknown list (all ten) and the five-question message; no risk read; display riskReadCopy.insufficient.

errorStates.condition: user looks for an eleventh custom claim or a free-text score field
errorStates.behavior: Not offered. Show: 'This tool checks the ten documented patterns from the companion article, not a general-purpose rating.'
Static HTML lists all ten claims with plain-language descriptions and the three answer states in a readable, unfiltered order.

privacyNote: The tool runs fully in the browser. The only free-text field is an optional, generic pitch label; no company name, personal name, email or address is requested. No data is transmitted or sent to a server. If answers are kept in localStorage for convenience, this is disclosed with a working 'Clear this pitch' control.
disclaimerText: This tool does not predict whether a GEO agency will perform well, and it is not legal advice. It only checks a pitch's claims against ten documented patterns: two that are false for any vendor, always, and eight that are common warning signs but not automatic disqualifiers on their own. It cannot verify anyone's honesty beyond the answers you enter, and it treats a pitch labelled 'Weissmann' exactly like any other.

primary.label: Run any GEO pitch, ours included, past a Weissmann call

secondary.label: Read the full checklist and the two claims that are always false
